samples.summary: The named-style registry is a third, unbanded read boundary for exactly the fontSize/lineHeight values this change bands elsewhere
samples.evidence: The change bands `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`padding`/image size at the two *tree-attribute* read boundaries (`crdt-tree.ts`, `YorkieDocStore.parseInlineStyle/parseBlockStyle`). But a resolved font size and line height do not only come from a block/inline attribute: `resolveStyleInline()` spreads `docStyles?.[id]?.inline` **last and unconditionally** (packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:272) and `resolveStyleBlock()` spreads `docStyles?.[id]?.block` (named-styles.ts:284), and `effectiveBlockSpacing` uses `styleBlock?.lineHeight` with no finiteness guard at all (named-styles.ts:640 — `authoredOr()` guards only the *block's own* value). That registry is read here as `JSON.parse(root.stylesJson) as DocStyles` with zero validation, and `root.stylesJson` is a peer-writable LWW CRDT root field. Attack: a collaborator with edit access writes `root.stylesJson = '{"normal":{"block":{"lineHeight":1e400},"inline":{"fontSize":1e400}}}'` — JSON.parse turns `1e400` into `Infinity` — and `assignLineHeights` computes `Math.max(1, Infinity) * maxFontSize` (packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:874-878), giving every line an Infinity height and `DocumentLayout.totalHeight = Infinity`. That is precisely the outcome the new module header calls unacceptable ("a bound in the paginator leaves the NaN geometry itself intact, which blanks the table … for every reader"), reached by a path with no band on it. A finite `1e300` is equally effective. No `normalizeFontSize`/`normalizeLineHeight` is applied on this path, and there is no DocStyles sanitizer anywhere.

samples.summary: `cols` / `columnWidths` is still read through `!isNaN`, which admits ±Infinity, two lines above the newly added `normalizeRowHeight` band
samples.evidence: `(attrs.cols ?? '').split(',').map(Number).filter((n) => !isNaN(n))` accepts `Infinity` and `-Infinity` (`!isNaN(Infinity) === true`), so a peer-written `cols="1e400"` (or literally `Infinity`) survives the only filter on this field. The value goes straight into geometry: `computeTableLayout` step 1 does `columnWidths.map((ratio) => ratio * contentWidth)` (packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:157), so `cellWidth`, `columnXOffsets`, `innerWidth` and `LayoutTable.totalWidth` all become non-finite and the table paints nothing for every reader — the same 'non-finite geometry blanks the content, and downstream Number.isFinite checks become meaningless' impact `row-height.ts` cites as its own justification. The identical parse exists in the live store (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:467), so both read boundaries the change hardened still let this one field through unbanded.

samples.summary: `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` is a per-row cap, not a global one, and the bands compose to ~10,600 px per single line — a hostile document can still multiply pages ~12–200×
samples.evidence: `paginatableRowHeight` clamps each row to `contentHeight * 200`, but nothing caps total pages, and the bands multiply: `MAX_FONT_SIZE` (400 pt) × `MAX_LINE_HEIGHT` (20) is a ~10,600 px line box, so one short line of text inside a table cell legitimately claims ~12 pages of `PageLine` objects, and one row can claim 200. A 500-row table with `rowHeights` at the in-band `MAX_ROW_HEIGHT` (10,000 px) is ~6,000 pages from ~500 tree nodes; using content-derived heights (17 in-band lines per cell) a ~8,500-block document reaches ~100,000 pages, each with its own `PageLine`. The module header claims each band 'is the range the editor's own controls can reach', but no control can produce fontSize 400 *and* lineHeight 20 together (the line-spacing menu tops out at 2), so the composed ceiling is ~10× looser than the stated invariant. Impact is a hang/OOM for every reader of a document one writer poisons — mitigated but not removed by the per-row bound.

samples.summary: The new read-side bands are narrower than a legitimate producer (DOCX import), so lawful content is silently mutated on the next read
samples.evidence: `normalizeFontSize` drops anything above 400 pt to `undefined` ('inherit'), and `normalizeLineHeight` anything above 20. The DOCX importer produces both without a ceiling: `style.fontSize = halfPointsToPoints(parseInt(val, 10))` (packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:50) — Word permits sizes far above 400 pt — and `layout.ts:869-872` documents that the import path 'can plant' large multipliers from `<w:spacing w:line="N" w:lineRule="exact"/>`. Such a document renders correctly in the importing session, is persisted verbatim, and then comes back from the CRDT with the size/leading dropped to the resolved default — silent, unrecoverable mutation of user content by a validator, not by an attacker. A clamp-to-ceiling (as `listLevel` and `rowHeights` do) would degrade instead of discarding.

samples.summary: The new `lineHeight` band falsifies the documented read/write symmetry with the v1 REST validator, which still accepts what the reader now drops
samples.evidence: The doc comment on `parseBlockStyleAttrs` asserts 'This also keeps the v1 REST endpoint's GET → PUT identity intact, since the validator on the write side rejects exactly the values dropped here.' The write-side validator only enforces finiteness (`typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value)` over `BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS`, packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:399-407), so a `PUT` with `style.lineHeight: 1e9` is accepted with a 200, persisted, and then silently dropped by the reader added here — the identity the comment claims no longer holds, and an API client's value disappears without any 400. Either the band belongs in `assertValidBlockStyle` too, or the comment's claim needs retracting.

samples.summary: `paginatableRowHeight` disables its own bound when `contentHeight <= 0`, returning the unbounded raw height
samples.evidence: `if (!(contentHeight > 0)) return raw;` hands the row-split loop an arbitrarily large finite height with no page bound, deliberately relying on the fragment loop's `if (!(fragHeight > 0)) fragHeight = remaining;` floor to terminate. I traced that it does terminate today (with `pageAvail <= 0` the loop takes `fragHeight = remaining` and exits in one iteration), and `resolvePageSetup`'s `fitMargins`/`MIN_CONTENT_PX` floor appears to make `contentHeight <= 0` unreachable in the first place — so this is a defensive branch whose defence is switched off exactly in the case it exists for. Worth deleting the branch or bounding with a constant instead, so the loop's guarantee does not depend on two cooperating fallbacks.

verdict.reason: The absence is real. `readDocStyles()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:687-696) and `docsTreeToDocument` (crdt-tree.ts:306-315) both decode the peer-writable `root.stylesJson` LWW field with nothing but a try/catch and a `typeof` check — no numeric band. The decoded registry then reaches geometry unguarded: `resolveStyleInline` spreads `docStyles[id].inline` last (named-styles.ts:269-273) into every run via `resolveBlockInlines` (layout.ts:165-172) and `getLineMaxFontSizePx` (layout.ts:1056-1075), while `effectiveBlockSpacing` takes `styleBlock?.lineHeight` verbatim (named-styles.ts:639-641) — `authoredOr` (named-styles.ts:598-600) guards only the block's own value — and `assignLineHeights` computes `Math.max(1, resolved.lineHeight) * maxFontSize` (layout.ts:873-878), so `{"normal":{"block":{"lineHeight":1e400},"inline":{"fontSize":1e400}}}` yields Infinity line heights and `totalHeight` (layout.ts:552,569) for every reader. I searched wide for a counterexample and found none: the bands in numeric-attrs.ts are called only from crdt-tree.ts:83, crdt-attrs.ts:149 and yorkie-doc-store.ts:200 (tree attributes); a full `sanitiz|isFinite` sweep of packages/docs/src and packages/frontend/src/app/docs, all DocStyles consumers, store/read-only.ts (pure access-control proxy), api/doc-styles.ts and the backend `@IsObject()`-only DTO show no DocStyles normalizer anywhere. pagination.ts:79-83 bounds only the table-row loop, the mitigation numeric-attrs.ts:20-26 explicitly calls insufficient. Untrusted-collaborator input reaching geometry is the same threat model the repo's own bands were written for, so it is in-lane (availability/integrity of the rendered document for all readers), major.

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists verbatim: packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:209-212 filters the peer-written `cols` attribute with only `!isNaN`, which admits `Infinity`/`-Infinity` (`Number('1e400') === Infinity`, `!isNaN(Infinity) === true`), and the value flows unmodified into `tableData.columnWidths` at line 229 — two lines below the newly added `normalizeRowHeight` band at 217-221. The identical unbanded parse exists on the live read boundary at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:467, beside its own hardened rowHeights path at 473-475. I enumerated all columnWidths readers (store/memory.ts:273, model/document.ts:947-1184, export/docx-exporter.ts:264,337, view/table-layout.ts:152-157) and all Number.isFinite sites in packages/docs/src; the only sanitizing readers are the paste path (view/clipboard.ts:70,289-294) and the DOCX import path (import/docx-importer.ts:273), neither of which covers the CRDT read boundary. pagination.ts:79-83 bands row height only. The lens applies: this is untrusted collaborator-controlled input reaching geometry unvalidated, the same threat model the repo's own row-height.ts:14-29 doc comment cites as justification for the band it adds.

finding.summary: The new row-height clamp does not close the paginator hang: `LayoutTable.rowHeights[r]` is also derived from cell content height, and an unvalidated `fontSize`/`padding`/`image.height` CRDT attribute still makes `while (consumed < rowHeight)` non-terminating for every reader
finding.evidence:
The delta's stated threat is "an `Infinity` height never terminates and a `1e9` one builds a million pages" (row-height.ts:20-29), and it clamps only the *user-specified minimum* at table-layout.ts:253 (step 5b raises the row height, never lowers it). The row height the paginator actually consumes is also produced by step 3/4 from cell content: `cellHeight = lines.reduce(...) + padding * 2` (table-layout.ts:196) → `rowHeights[r] = Math.max(rowHeights[r], cell.height)` (table-layout.ts:213). Those inputs are read from CRDT attributes with no bound at all:
  • `style.fontSize = Number(attrs.fontSize)` — packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:72 and the frontend twin packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:192
  • `style.padding = Number(attrs.padding)` — crdt-tree.ts:131 / yorkie-doc-store.ts:311
  • `image.height` is checked finite but unbounded — crdt-tree.ts:80-86 (1e9 is accepted)
  • block `lineHeight` is checked finite but unbounded — crdt-attrs.ts:137-138, used as `Math.max(1, resolved.lineHeight) * maxFontSize` at layout.ts:874-878.
Attack: a collaborator (or any client that can PUT doc content) writes `fontSize="Infinity"` on an inline node inside a table cell, or `padding="Infinity"` on the cell node. Reader path: treeNodeToBlock → parseInlineStyle/parseCellStyle → Infinity → `ptToPx(Infinity)` = Infinity → line.height = Infinity → cell.height = Infinity → `rowHeights[r] = Infinity` (untouched by step 5b) → pagination.ts:99 `currentY + rowHeight <= contentHeight` is false → pagination.ts:124 `while (consumed < Infinity)`: each iteration `fragHeight = Math.min(remaining, pageAvail)` = one content height, so `consumed` grows by ~864 forever while a `startNewPage()`/`PageLine` is pushed per iteration → hang and unbounded memory growth in every reader's tab (and in any Node-side paginating export). A finite `fontSize="1e9"` or `image.height=1e9` gives the ~1.1M-page OOM variant. The poisoned attribute persists in the CRDT, so every reload re-hangs. The

verdict.reason: The finding's central premise — that the only clamp is on the user-specified row-height minimum, leaving content-derived heights to hang `while (consumed < rowHeight)` — is contradicted by the file it names. `pagination.ts:79-83` defines `paginatableRowHeight`, which returns 0 for non-finite/<=0 and otherwise `Math.min(raw, contentHeight * MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN)` (MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN = 200, pagination.ts:67), and it is applied at pagination.ts:132 to `tl.rowHeights[ri]` before the split loop at pagination.ts:161. Its doc comment (pagination.ts:52-65) states outright that the bound exists precisely because steps 3-4 of computeTableLayout derive the height from cell content. So `Infinity` yields rowHeight 0 (loop not entered) and 1e9 is capped at ~200 pages. Separately, each of the four attribute reads the finding cites as "unbounded" is in fact banded at BOTH read boundaries: fontSize via normalizeFontSize (crdt-tree.ts:82-85, yorkie-doc-store.ts:199-201), cell padding via normalizeCellPadding (crdt-tree.ts:145-147, yorkie-doc-store.ts:322-324), image height via isPaintableImageSize which enforces `height <= MAX_IMAGE_SIZE` so 1e9 is rejected not accepted (crdt-tree.ts:96-97, numeric-attrs.ts:102-110), and block lineHeight via normalizeLineHeight banded to (0,20] (crdt-attrs.ts:148-152, numeric-attrs.ts:71-77). The claimed vector is blocked twice independently, and the quoted evidence lines do not contain the code attributed to them.

finding.summary: No normalizer for the sibling unvalidated numeric CRDT attributes (`fontSize`, cell `padding`, `image.height`, block `lineHeight`) at the same read boundary the delta hardens, leaving the same hostile-collaborator vector open
finding.evidence: This delta adds `normalizeRowHeight` and applies it at both Tree read boundaries (crdt-tree.ts:203, yorkie-doc-store.ts:460), mirroring `normalizeListLevel`. The neighbouring numeric attributes read in the same functions have no equivalent: crdt-tree.ts:72 (`fontSize = Number(...)`, so `NaN`/`Infinity`/1e9 all reach layout), crdt-tree.ts:131 (`padding = Number(...)`), crdt-tree.ts:80-86 (`image.width/height` finite-checked but unbounded), crdt-attrs.ts:135-139 (`lineHeight`/`marginTop`/`marginLeft` finite-checked but unbounded). Each feeds the same geometry the row-height band exists to protect (see the linked finding on pagination.ts:124), so the documented invariant "bounding it here bounds all of them" (table-layout.ts:250) does not hold. A `fontSize`/`padding` band applied in these two parsers — plus a finite/ceiling guard where `LayoutTable.rowHeights` is finalized (table-layout.ts:305-322) — is what would make the claim true.

verdict.reason: The "missing" normalizers exist in packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts (normalizeFontSize, normalizeLineHeight, normalizeCellPadding, isPaintableImageSize, with MAX_FONT_SIZE/MAX_LINE_HEIGHT/MAX_CELL_PADDING/MAX_IMAGE_SIZE), and are applied at exactly the two read boundaries the finding names: fontSize at crdt-tree.ts:82-85 and yorkie-doc-store.ts:200; cell padding at crdt-tree.ts:145-148 and yorkie-doc-store.ts:323; image width/height ceiling via isPaintableImageSize at crdt-tree.ts:95-97 and yorkie-doc-store.ts:217; block lineHeight via normalizeLineHeight at crdt-attrs.ts:148-152. The finding's quoted evidence lines are misreads (crdt-tree.ts:72 is `underline`, :131 is the border-width parse inside parseBorderStyle). The bands are re-exported from both package entries (index.ts:101-104, node.ts:145-148) and unit-tested (test/model/numeric-attrs.test.ts:35-43). Only marginTop/marginLeft remain finite-checked-but-unbounded (crdt-attrs.ts:136-139); those are additive offsets, not the font-size/line-height/padding multiplier chain the finding's hang vector depends on, so they do not sustain the absence claim.
